human (192)R and (192)Q paraoxonases are different in their hydrolytic activities against phenylacetate and homocysteinethiolactone.
human serum PON1 hydrolyzes homocysteic thiolactone and that (192)R isoenzyme is more efficient than (192)Q isoenzyme in the hydrolysis reaction.

the identification of a new role for PON1 as a potential regulator of homocysteinemia.
the purification of PON1 isozymes and their characterization with respect to their catalytic activity.
the identification of the physiological role of PON1 and the elucidation of its molecular mechanism.
